[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p21/r2] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · الزمخشري | reports | Al-Zamakhsharī glosses قد نرى as perhaps seeing, then says the construction conveys frequent seeing, comparing it with قد أترك.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p21/r3] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | rejects | Abū Ḥayyān rejects that explanation: perhaps usually conveys rarity, so it conflicts with the claim of frequency.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p21/r4] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | The word قد itself does not indicate frequency; repeated seeing is inferred from تقلب, since turning one's gaze entails repeated movements.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p21/r5] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | Repeated movement is conveyed by تقلب, the reciprocal result of repeatedly turning the gaze, as in cutting until something is cut or breaking until it breaks.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p21/r6] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | reports | One view takes وجه in its apparent, literal sense.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p21/r7] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · قتادة، السدي وغيرهما | reports | Qatada, al-Suddī, and others say the Messenger repeatedly looked toward heaven while praying that God turn him toward Mecca.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p21/r8] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | reports | Another view says he looked toward the sky in order to be permitted to pray.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p21/r9] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · الزمخشري | reports | Al-Zamakhsharī says the Prophet expected a change to the Kaaba, Abraham's qibla, which would attract Arabs through their pride and pilgrimage sites and oppose the Jews.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p22/r1] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | The phrase is not an ellipsis for بصر وجهك: Arabic says your sight, eye, or nose, not the sight, eye, or nose of your face.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p22/r10] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | The object of رضاه i

[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p22/r2] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | In the preferred syntax, في السماء modifies the verbal noun تقلب and في retains its ordinary meaning; a Qur'anic parallel uses the same preposition. | mentions 3:196
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p22/r3] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | reports | One alternative takes في to mean إلى, so the phrase means toward the sky.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p22/r4] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | reports | Another analysis attaches في السماء to نرى and takes في to mean من, meaning God sees the turning from heaven; the wording magnifies the event without implying divine localization.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p22/r5] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | Abū Ḥayyān prefers attachment to تقلب with في literal; the sky is linked to mercy and blessings, supplication, and the expected descent of Gabriel.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p22/r6] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | فلنولينك implies an omitted state: the Prophet was turning his face skyward while seeking another qibla.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p22/r7] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | The promise is made under an unspoken oath to emphasize that it will be fulfilled.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p22/r8] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | The promise precedes the command to delight the Prophet first by the response and again by its fulfillment; a promised result is also more reassuring than a sudden one.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p22/r9] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | قبلة is indefinite because no antecedent makes it definite; رضاه nearly identifies the qibla, revealing the Prophet's inward preference for the Kaaba although he did not say so explicitly.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p23/r1] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | reports | The Prophet's approval of the Kaaba may stem from natural inclination or from the religious benefits it contains.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p23/r10] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · الجبائي، القاضي | reports | Al-Jubbāʾī and the Qāḍī understand شطر as the middle of the mosque, where the Kaaba stands, and argue that the command requires facing that point.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p23/r11] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · الجبائي، القاضي | reports | Their argument is that facing the mosque while missing its center would invalidate prayer; reading شطر as merely a side would add nothing and fail to require facing the Kaaba.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p23/r12] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · ابن عباس وغيرُه | reports | Ibn Abbas and others say the Messenger was directed toward the entire House.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p23/r13] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · ابن عمر | reports | Ibn ʿUmar says the Prophet and his community faced the line of the Kaaba's waterspout, the qibla for Medina, Syria, and approximately Andalusia.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p23/r14] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | There is no disagreement that the Kaaba is the qibla for people in every region.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p23/r15] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · عبد الله | reports | The reading attributed to ʿAbd Allāh has تلقاء in place of شطر.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p23/r16] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · ابن عباس، مالك | reports | Ibn Abbas's hierarchy, also attributed to Mālik, makes the House the qibla for mosque-goers, the mosque for people of the sanctuary, and the sanctuary for people in east and west.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p23/r17] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | reports | Others say the Kaaba itself is the qibla; Abū Ḥayyān takes the apparent meaning of شطر as direction, since exact alignment would burden those far away.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p23/r18] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | Mentioning the Sacred Mosque instead of the Kaaba indicates that the obligation is to face the Kaaba's direction rather than its precise point.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p23/r19] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · مالك | reports | Mālik infers from the command to face the mosque that a worshipper looks ahead rather than at the place of prostration.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p23/r2] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | The promise means God will make the Prophet lead the community toward a qibla pleasing to him and enable him to do so.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p23/r20] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · الثوري، الشافعي، الحسن بن حي | reports | Al-Thawrī, al-Shāfiʿī, and al-Ḥasan ibn Ḥayy prefer looking at the place of prostration.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p23/r21] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · شريك القاضي | reports | Sharīk al-Qāḍī prescribes different sightlines: prostration spot while standing, feet in bowing, nose in prostration, and lap while seated.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p23/r3] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | The command فول وجهك شطر المسجد الحرام means to turn toward the Kaaba during prayer.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p23/r4] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | This command abrogated facing Jerusalem.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p23/r5] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | reports | Some say the verse omits mention of prayer because it was revealed while the Prophet was praying; others say prayer is implicit because that is the only intended context.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p23/r6] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | prefers | Abū Ḥayyān argues that the preceding promise of a qibla the Prophet approves already shows that prayer is intended.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p23/r7] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | وجه means the whole body, since the entire body must face the qibla; the face can stand for the whole because it is the noblest and most identifying part.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p23/r8] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | The wording may also mean the thing itself and pairs the turning of the face with the command to turn it.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p23/r9] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · الجمهور، الشافعي | reports | Most exegetes, with al-Shāfiʿī, understand شطر as toward or the side of the mosque.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p24/r1] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | The Prophet should look ahead: lowering the head compromises upright posture, while keeping it erect and looking down is severe hardship, which religion removes. | mentions 22:78
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p24/r10] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | Those described as recipients of scripture are the leading Jews and Christians and their learned authorities.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p24/r11] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · السدي | reports | Al-Suddī identifies the recipients of scripture here as the Jews.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p24/r12] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | What they know to be true is facing the Sacred Mosque, the direction God prescribed for Abraham and his descendants.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p24/r13] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · قتادة والضحاك | reports | Qatāda and al-Ḍaḥḥāk say the qibla meant is the Kaaba.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p24/r14] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · الكسائي | reports | Al-Kisāʾī takes the pronoun to refer to shatr, meaning the direction, close to the preceding explanation.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p24/r15] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · قتادة ومجاهد | reports | Another view, also given by Qatāda and Mujāhid, takes the pronoun as Muhammad: they know his truthfulness and prophethood.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p24/r2] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | Wherever you are covers every place a person may inhabit.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p24/r3] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | Grammatically, ḥaythu is initially a place adverb with a genitive complement; adding mā removes annexation, gives it conditional force, and lets it govern the verbs.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p24/r4] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | The command to face the Sacred Mosque applies equally to Muhammad and his community, avoiding any impression that the ruling was exclusive to him.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p24/r5] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | The command is general across the earth, so the qibla is not restricted to Medina.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p24/r6] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | The Prophet is addressed first because he longed for the change; the community follows him, and this order prevents assuming the command was his alone.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p24/r7] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | reports | The reading attributed to ʿAbd Allāh says ‘toward it’ instead of ‘toward its direction.’
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p24/r8] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · ابن أبي عبلة | reports | Ibn Abī ʿAbla reads ‘in its direction’; these variants show that shatr means toward or in the direction of something.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p24/r9] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | The intended sense of shatr is direction or towardness.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p25/r1] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | The Messenger pronoun refers to his own address; under this analysis the passage contains two shifts in address.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p25/r10] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | reports | Ibn ʿĀmir, Ḥamza, and al-Kisāʾī read the closing verb with second-person tāʾ.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p25/r11] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | reports | With the second-person reading, the addressees may be believers, following the preceding command to face the mosque.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p25/r12] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | reports | Alternatively, the second-person reading addresses the People of the Book, shifting from third-person reference to direct speech.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p25/r13] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | Direct address urges the People of the Book to act on the truth they know; confrontation intensifies blame and underscores the matter's gravity.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p25/r14] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | reports | Readers using third-person yāʾ most naturally refer to the People of the Book, continuing the surrounding third-person discourse.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p25/r15] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | Either reading warns that God does not overlook people's deeds.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p25/r2] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | Abū Ḥayyān notes that this analysis of the pronouns yields two shifts in address.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p25/r3] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | The verb ‘know’ may take two objects or one

[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p25/r4] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · أبو العالية | reports | Abū al-ʿĀliya says they knew from their scripture that the direction was toward the Kaaba.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p25/r5] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | reports | Another explanation is that their scripture identifies Muhammad as a true prophet who commands only what is right.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p25/r6] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | reports | A further basis for their knowledge is that abrogation is permissible.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p25/r7] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | reports | They may also know because prophetic glad tidings said the Messenger would pray facing both qiblas.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p25/r8] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | ‘From their Lord’ is a circumstantial phrase meaning that the truth is established by their Lord; the change was commanded by God, not reached through ijtihād.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p25/r9] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | Calling God ‘their Lord’ signals that one must follow truth established by the one who cares for one's reform, as ‘the truth is from your Lord’ says. | mentions 2:147
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p7/r3] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | Al-ḥarām and al-ḥaram denote what is prohibited or inaccessible.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p8/r2] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · البراء بن عازب | reports | The Prophet faced Jerusalem for sixteen or seventeen months after arriving in Medina, wished to face the Kaaba, and then received the revelation directing him toward it; Jews asked what had turned them from their former qibla. | mentions 2:144
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p8/r4] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · الزمخشري | reports | On the apparent future reading, God foretold the Jews' objection before the order to face the Kaaba, making it a prediction of the unseen and preparing the Prophet and Muslims for the objection with an answer ready. | mentions 2:144
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p8/r5] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · ابن عباس | reports | An alternative chronology places the order to face the Kaaba before this verse in revelation, although this verse comes first in the recitation; Ibn Abbas and others state this, and the Barāʾ report supports it. | mentions 2:144
[SAMIN-DURR:2:144#2/r1] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | prefers | في may attach to verbal noun تقلب with ordinary locative sense; it may mean إلى, but al-Samīn sees no need because this noun is attested with في, as in 3:196. | mentions 3:196
[SAMIN-DURR:2:144#2/r2] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | reports | A second view attaches في to نرى and takes في to mean من; heaven is mentioned honorifically, not to claim God occupies a direction.
[SAMIN-DURR:2:144#2/r3] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · أبو البقاء | reports | Abu al-Baqāʾ makes في السماء an accusative حال from وجهك, attached to an omitted element.
[SAMIN-DURR:2:144#2/r4] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | holds | تقلب is annexed to its subject; it cannot be annexed to its object, for that verbal noun would be التقليب.
[SAMIN-DURR:2:144#2/r5] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | holds | There is no need to supply an omitted مضاف meaning sight of your face, a rare usage; face is the noblest feature and one turned by a petitioner, though another view takes it as metonym for sight.
[SAMIN-DURR:2:144#3/r1] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | holds | The فاء marks consequence, and the clause answers an omitted oath, فوالله لنولينك.
[SAMIN-DURR:2:144#3/r2] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | holds | نولي governs two objects, the suffix ك and قبلة; ترضاها is a clause in the accusative qualifying قبلة.
[SAMIN-DURR:2:144#3/r3] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · الشيخ | reports | The shaykh says the promise implies an omitted حال: God sees the Prophet turning his face toward heaven while seeking a different qibla from the one he faces.
[SAMIN-DURR:2:144#3/r4] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | prefers | ولي governs وجهك and شطر as two objects; it can also take its second object with إلى.
[SAMIN-DURR:2:144#3/r5] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · النحاس | reports | Al-Naḥḥās allows شطر as locative adverb, leaving ولي with one object; al-Zamakhsharī mentions only that analysis, but al-Samīn finds the two-object analysis clearer.
[SAMIN-DURR:2:144#3/r6] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | holds | شطر can mean half or part, or direction and toward; lines 762–767 attest the directional sense, including Ibn Aḥmar's شطر نجد.
[SAMIN-DURR:2:144#3/r7] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · ابن أحمر | reports | Ibn Aḥmar's شطر نجد means toward Najd and witnesses the directional sense of شطر.
[SAMIN-DURR:2:144#3/r8] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | holds | شطر also means far away: الشاطر is a youth distant from neighbors and home, شطير is distant, and شطر إليه can mean turning toward; al-Rāghib also uses الشاطر for distancing from truth, plural شطار.
[SAMIN-DURR:2:144#4/r1] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | prefers | The clearest analysis takes ḥaythumā as conditional; the added mā is required for that force, contrary to al-Farrāʾ.
[SAMIN-DURR:2:144#4/r2] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | holds | On the conditional analysis, kuntum is jussive, wallū answers the condition, and ḥaythumā is an accusative adverb governed by kuntum; Q 17:110 illustrates the construction. | mentions 17:110
[SAMIN-DURR:2:144#4/r3] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · الشيخ | reports | Although ḥayth is a locative noun normally annexed to a clause in the genitive, its connection with mā removes annexation and gives it conditional force and verbal governance.
[SAMIN-DURR:2:144#4/r4] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · أبو البقاء | rejects | Abū al-Baqāʾ treats ḥayth as a nonconditional adverb governed by wallū; the author rejects this because added mā necessarily makes it conditional.
[SAMIN-DURR:2:144#4/r5] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | holds | Wallū derives from waliyū: the heavy ḍamma on yā is dropped, then yā is deleted at the meeting of two sukūns and the preceding vowel is rounded to match the pronoun.
[SAMIN-DURR:2:144#4/r6] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | reports | Shatrahu has two analyses: it is either the direct object or an adverb of direction, as discussed earlier.
[SAMIN-DURR:2:144#5/r1] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · الجمهور | reports | For the majority, the clause anna-hu al-ḥaqq supplies both objects of yaʿlamūn.
[SAMIN-DURR:2:144#5/r2] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · الأخفش | reports | Al-Akhfash allows the clause to supply one object of a verb taking two, with the second object omitted.
[SAMIN-DURR:2:144#5/r3] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | reports | A further analysis has the clause supply one object because yaʿlamūn means to recognize or know.
[SAMIN-DURR:2:144#5/r4] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | reports | One proposed antecedent of the pronoun in annahu is the turning toward the qibla implied by wallū.
[SAMIN-DURR:2:144#5/r5] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | reports | A second proposed antecedent of the pronoun in annahu is the direction, shatrahu.
[SAMIN-DURR:2:144#5/r6] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | reports | A third view refers the pronoun to the Prophet; this shifts from direct address in fa-lanuwalliyannaka to speaking of him in the third person.
[SAMIN-DURR:2:144#5/r7] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | holds | Min rabbihim modifies an omitted circumstantial expression describing al-ḥaqq: the truth is from their Lord.
[SAMIN-DURR:2:144#5/r8] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | reports | The third-person reading may address the People of the Book or refer back to the believers, with a shift from the preceding address.
[SAMIN-DURR:2:144#5/r9] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | reports | The direct-address reading most naturally addresses the believers; it may instead turn to the People of the Book to spur them on.
[SAMIN-DURR:2:144/r1] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | reports | Some grammarians say قد shifts a present verb into past meaning, applying it here and citing poetry with قد نرى أمس.
[SAMIN-DURR:2:144/r2] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · الزمخشري | reports | Al-Zamakhsharī glosses قد نرى as perhaps we see and takes it to suggest abundant seeing, citing قد أترك القرن.
[SAMIN-DURR:2:144/r3] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · الشيخ | rejects | The shaykh says al-Zamakhsharī contradicts himself: ربما suggests rarity on the relevant account, not abundance; قد itself does not encode abundance, which comes from repeated turning being seen.
[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p458/r1] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · ابن عباس | reports | Ibn ʿAbbas says the qibla was the first Qur'anic abrogation: after migration, the Prophet faced Jerusalem for over a year at God's command, though he loved Abraham's qibla and prayed looking skyward; the change unsettled the Jews, and God had tested who followed the Messenger. | mentions 2:142, 2:115, 2:143
[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p458/r2] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · ابن عباس | reports | Another Ibn ʿAbbas report says that after praying toward Jerusalem the Prophet raised his head to heaven; God revealed the change toward the Kaaba, with Gabriel directing him toward its water-spout.
[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p458/r3] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · عبد الله بن عمرو | reports | Yahya b. Qumta saw ʿAbd Allah b. ʿAmr facing toward the Kaaba's mizab and explaining that the commanded direction was toward it; al-Hakim graded the chain sound and said the two compilers did not include it.
[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p458/r4] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · الشافعي | reports | One of al-Shafiʿi's two positions requires facing the Kaaba itself, based on reports specifying its line or the direction of its mizab.
[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p458/r5] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · الأكثرون | prefers | The majority position, also attributed to al-Shafiʿi, requires facing the Kaaba's direction; Ali glosses shatr as its qibla, and al-Hakim grades the report sound.
